Definition: Midjan, a son of Abraham; also his country and (collectively) his descendants
BiblicalUsage: Midian was the fourth son of Keturah, born to Abraham after Sarah's death. Moses fled to the land of Midian and sat down by a well, and in the days of the judges the Lord delivered Israel into the hand of Midian for seven years. The name covers the man, the land, and the people.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Midian's story is the story of a kinsman turned enemy: Abraham's son became the land where Moses hid, and the people who oppressed Israel until Gideon.
